paragraphs: As used in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, unless the context indicates or otherwise requires, "Design," "our company," "we," "us," and "our" refer to Design Therapeutics, Inc., a Delaware corporation.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering the research and development of GeneTAC® molecules, which are a novel class of small-molecule gene targeted chimera therapeutic candidates designed to be disease-modifying by addressing the underlying cause of diseases caused by inherited nucleotide repeat expansion mutations. Certain diseases caused by inherited nucleotide repeat expansion, such as Friedreich ataxia (FA) and fragile X syndrome, can result in reduced gene expression and deficiency of vital proteins; in other diseases, such as myotonic dystrophy type-1 (DM1), Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD), and Huntington's disease (HD), the nucleotide repeat expansions result in the generation of toxic gene products, often associated with pathological nuclear foci and broad splicing disruptions or the expression of mutant proteins that form toxic aggregates. Our GeneTAC® small molecules are designed to selectively target expanded genetic repeat sequences, modulate gene expression either by dialing up or down mRNA transcription, depending on the cause of the disease, and restore cellular health. As a platform, we believe that GeneTAC® molecules have broad potential applicability across currently unaddressed degenerative, monogenic nucleotide repeat expansion diseases affecting millions of individuals worldwide.

In preclinical studies for our lead program in FA, we have observed restoration of frataxin (FXN) levels in multiple cell types from FA patients and an in vivo murine model of FA using our FA GeneTAC® molecules. At doses that were observed to be well-tolerated in rodents and non-human primates (NHPs), FA GeneTAC® molecules achieved biodistribution to brain and heart, key organs affected by FA, at concentrations that exceeded those observed to restore FXN levels in FA patient cells. Further, and consistent with this favorable target-organ biodistribution, we observed increased endogenous FXN expression in the brain and heart in an animal model of FA after treatment with our FA GeneTAC® molecules. Previously, we reported clinical data for our lead FA GeneTAC® small molecule, DT-216, formulated as the prior DT-216 product candidate (DT-216P1) from a Phase 1 single-ascending dose (SAD) clinical trial in December 2022 and a Phase 1 multiple-ascending dose (MAD) clinical trial in August 2023. Both studies showed that DT-216 was generally well-tolerated and exhibited the ability to overcome the FXN transcription impairment that causes FA. Data from the Phase 1 MAD clinical trial for DT-216P1 suggests more sustained exposure to DT-216 is likely needed to achieve a more durable increase in FXN expression. We then shifted focus to developing DT-216 with a potentially improved formulation to enable more sustained exposure for the treatment of FA. These efforts resulted in a new product candidate, DT-216P2, which uses the same drug substance, DT-216. In nonclinical studies, we observed higher and more sustained DT-216 plasma levels after administration of DT-216P2 than was seen in studies with DT-216P1.

A Phase 1 SAD clinical trial of DT-216P2 in normal healthy volunteers to evaluate single doses using multiple routes of administration, specifically IV infusion and subcutaneous (SC) injection and infusion routes, has shown that DT-216P2 has been generally well-tolerated. Human plasma pharmacokinetics (PK) profiles of DT-216P2 were consistent with NHP data following both IV and SC single-dose administration and human PK data has demonstrated that DT-216P2 exhibited improved exposure and PK parameters compared to DT-216P1, including higher area under the curve (AUC) and sustained plasma levels at comparable doses.

We are conducting our RESTORE-FA (Reactivating Expression Suppressed Through Overcoming Repeat Expansion for FA) Phase 1/2 MAD clinical trial of DT-216P2. The RESTORE-FA trial is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK and pharmacodynamics (PD) of IV and SC of DT-216P2 in patients with FA. We anticipate providing an update from the RESTORE-FA trial on the effect of DT-216P2 on endogenous frataxin levels following 12 weeks of dosing in the second half of 2026.

In June 2025, we received a clinical hold notice from the FDA regarding our IND application for DT-216P2. In December 2025, the clinical hold was lifted and we received clearance from the FDA to initiate clinical studies for DT-216P2.

In December 2022, we nominated our second GeneTAC® small molecule, DT-168, an eye drop for the treatment of FECD. When tested in vitro in FECD patient-derived corneal endothelial cells, our FECD GeneTAC® molecules led to robust reductions in the pathogenic nuclear RNA foci and corrected key mis-spliced transcripts to levels observed in control corneal endothelial cells from unaffected donors. DT-168 was well-tolerated and distribution of DT-168 was observed in and through the cornea in animal models after administration via eye drop. In addition, DT-168 has been evaluated in chronic toxicity studies of up to nine months in duration. We believe these preclinical data support the potential of our novel GeneTAC® small molecules to correct the most common underlying genetic cause of FECD. We are currently conducting an observational study in FECD to confirm disease characteristics and evaluate deterioration in the context of running a trial and to identify characteristics of FECD patients at risk of more rapid disease progression. We have achieved our enrollment goal for the observational study by recruiting and completing baseline assessments on approximately 250 FECD patients. Based on the baseline characteristics data, we have chosen approximately 100 patients for future follow-up visits. This will inform our clinical development efforts and we believe it could potentially increase the probability of DT-168 programmatic success.

In May 2025, we reported results from a completed Phase 1, double-masked, placebo-controlled, randomized, SAD/MAD clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability and systemic PK of DT-168 ophthalmic solution in normal healthy volunteers. DT-168 eye drops were well-tolerated in all participants with a maximum dose of two 0.5% drops twice-daily for seven days. There were no serious adverse events, no ocular adverse events (AEs) and no treatment discontinuations due to AEs in the trial. All observed AEs were deemed not related to DT-168 by the trial investigator. In parallel with the Phase 1 trial, we conducted reference range studies which showed consistently different splicing in the corneal endothelium between unaffected eye donors and surgical samples from mutant TCF4 FECD patients, supporting the potential for corneal endothelium biomarkers as a clinical proof-of-concept measure of drug activity. We are conducting a Phase 2 biomarker trial of DT-168 to evaluate safety, tolerability, and corneal endothelium biomarkers in patients with FECD. We anticipate reporting data from the Phase 2 biomarker trial in the second half of 2026.

In the fourth quarter of 2025, we announced DT-818 as our GeneTAC® small molecule development candidate for the treatment of DM1. In preclinical studies, DT-818 has demonstrated a potential best-in-disease profile for DM1, including a greater than 90% reduction in toxic RNA foci in DM1 patient cells, corresponding splicing correction and selective targeting of mutant DMPK. In an actin repeat mouse model of DM1 (HSALR mouse model), DT-818 treatment resulted in improved myotonia and foci reduction. In tissue distribution studies in NHPs, DT-818 levels were observed to be at expected pharmacologic levels in key target tissues at well-tolerated doses. In the fourth quarter of 2025, we obtained regulatory clearance to initiate clinical development of DT-818 and plan to begin dosing DM1 patients in a Phase 1 MAD trial in the first half of 2026. The study, with results anticipated in 2027, is expected to assess safety and correction of mis-splicing.

Our fourth program based on the GeneTAC® platform is focused on HD. We are currently conducting preclinical studies on promising HD GeneTAC® candidate molecules. We have observed reduced mutant huntingtin (mtHTT) mRNA and protein and preservation of wild type huntingtin (wtHTT) in HD patient cells after treatment with our HD GeneTAC® candidate molecules. In in vivo studies in zQ175DN mice, an animal model of HD, we observed a reduction of over 50% in mtHTT mRNA and protein in the brain striatum after eight weeks of systemic administration of our HD GeneTAC® candidate molecules. In the same study, wtHTT mRNA and protein levels were shown to be preserved after treatment with our HD GeneTAC® candidate molecules. We plan to continue to evaluate these HD candidate molecules in nonclinical studies. The final development candidate will be based on the molecules that perform favorably in relevant studies.

We have continued to make significant progress in advancing our GeneTAC® portfolio in preclinical studies to address other diseases and intend to declare additional product candidates as they progress towards the clinic.

We believe the structure and mechanism of action of our GeneTAC® molecules may offer the disease-modifying potential of genomic therapeutics, while also offering broad tissue biodistribution, resolution of aberrant gene expression preserving endogenous regulatory control elements, and leveraging established manufacturing, regulatory, and distribution frameworks for small molecules.

We utilize our proprietary GeneTAC® platform to design and develop therapeutic candidates for inherited diseases driven by nucleotide repeat expansion. Individuals with nucleotide repeat expansion diseases are born with abnormally expanded stretches of specific nucleotide sequences, often with hundreds to thousands of excess repeats present in the mutant gene. Higher number of excess repeats can lead to more severe, and sometimes a more rapidly progressive form of disease. Nucleotide repeat expansion has been identified as the underlying cause of more than 40 debilitating degenerative diseases impacting millions of people. Currently, there are no approved therapeutic options that address the cause of any nucleotide repeat expansion diseases.

Specific DNA sequences of a gene can generate RNA through a process called transcription. The RNA is, in turn, used as a template to make the proteins that control cellular functions in a process called translation. Combined, transcription and translation are responsible for gene expression. Individuals who have a nucleotide repeat expansion in the DNA can experience different alterations of transcription. In some diseases such as FA, the transcription machinery stalls at the abnormally expanded repeat sequence leading to insufficient production of a critical protein called FXN. In other cases, such as in DM1, the abnormal RNA transcript arising from the nucleotide repeat expansion mutation is misprocessed, leading to a cascade of downstream toxicity and cellular dysfunction.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Position and Capital Requirements
If we are unable to raise additional capital when needed, we may be forced to delay, reduce or eliminate our product development programs or other operations.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or product candidates.
Our financial condition could be adversely affected if the financial institutions in which we hold our cash fail.
Risks Related to the Discovery, Development and Regulatory Approval of Our Product Candidates

Our product candidates are based on novel technologies, which make it difficult to predict the timing, results and cost of product candidate development and likelihood of obtaining regulatory approval.
If we encounter difficulties or delays enrolling patients in our clinical trials, our clinical development activities could be delayed or otherwise adversely affected.
We are conducting and plan to conduct additional clinical trials for our product candidates outside the United States and the FDA may not accept data from such trials.

Obtaining and maintaining regulatory approval of our product candidates in one jurisdiction does not mean that we will be successful in obtaining regulatory approval of our product candidates in other jurisdictions.
International trade policies, including tariffs, sanctions and trade barriers may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.
paragraphs: We operate in a dynamic and rapidly changing environment that involves numerous risks and uncertainties. Certain factors may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations, and you should carefully consider them. Accordingly, in evaluating our business, we encourage you to consider the following discussion of risks described below, together with the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and in our other public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future growth prospects would likely be materially and adversely affected. In these circumstances, the market price of our common stock would likely decline. Other events that we do not currently anticipate or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our results of operations and financial condition.

We have a limited operating history, have incurred net losses since our inception, and anticipate that we will continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future. We may never generate any revenue or become profitable or, if we achieve profitability, may not be able to sustain it.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with a limited operating history that may make it difficult to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability. Our operations to date have been limited to business planning, organizing and staffing our company, raising capital, developing and optimizing our technology platform, identifying potential product candidates, undertaking research and nonclinical studies for our lead program in FA and our other development programs, early clinical development for our FA, FECD and DM1 programs, establishing and enhancing our intellectual property portfolio, and providing general and administrative support for these operations. As a result, none of our product candidates have been approved for commercial sale. We have never generated any revenue from product sales and have incurred net losses each year since we commenced operations, including a net loss of $69.8 million and $49.6 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. We expect that it will be several years, if ever, before we have a product candidate ready for regulatory approval and commercialization. We expect to incur increasing levels of operating losses over the next several years and for the foreseeable future as we advance our product candidates through clinical development. Our prior losses, combined with expected future losses, have had and will continue to have an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital.

To become and remain profitable, we must develop and eventually commercialize a product or products with significant market potential. This will require us to be successful in a range of challenging activities, including completing nonclinical studies and clinical trials of our product candidates, obtaining marketing approval for these product candidates, manufacturing, marketing and selling those products for which we may obtain marketing approval and satisfying any post-marketing requirements. We may never succeed in these activities and, even if we succeed in commercializing one or more of our product candidates, we may never generate revenue that is significant or large enough to achieve profitability. In addition, as a young business, we may encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays and other known and unknown challenges. If we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis and we will continue to incur substantial research and development and other expenditures to develop and market additional product candidates. Our failure to become and remain profitable would decrease the value of the company and could impair our ability to raise capital, maintain our research and development efforts, expand our business or continue our operations. A decline in the value of our company could also cause you to lose all or part of your investment.

Since our inception, we have used substantial amounts of cash to fund our operations and expect our expenses to increase substantially during the next few years. The development of biopharmaceutical product candidates is capital intensive. As our product candidates enter and advance through nonclinical studies and clinical trials, we will need substantial additional funds to expand our clinical, regulatory, quality and manufacturing capabilities. In addition, if we obtain marketing approval for any of our product candidates, we expect to incur significant commercialization expenses related to marketing, sales, manufacturing and distribution.

As of December 31, 2025, we had $219.8 million in cash, cash equivalents and investment securities. Based upon our current operating plan, we estimate that our existing cash, cash equivalents and investment securities will be sufficient to fund our operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements for more than the next 12 months. However, we believe that our existing cash, cash equivalents and investment securities will not be sufficient to fund any of our product candidates through regulatory approval, and we will need to raise substantial additional capital to complete the development and commercialization of our product candidates.

疾病。目前對於疾病修正療法仍存在高度未滿足的醫療需求，本公司認為本公司 FA GeneTAC® 分子具有高度吸引力且差異化的特性。
paragraphs: 本年度報告書（Form 10-K）中所使用的「Design」、「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們」，除非上下文另有明確指示或需要，否則均指 Design Therapeutics, Inc.，一家設立於特拉華州的公司。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物製藥公司，專注於研發 GeneTAC® 分子，這是一種新型的小分子基因靶向嵌合體治療候選藥物，設計用以透過解決遺傳性核苷酸重複擴展突變所導致的疾病根源，來改變疾病的進程。某些由遺傳性核苷酸重複擴展所引起的疾病，例如弗裏德賴希共濟失調症（FA）和脆X症候羣，可能會導致基因表達減少及關鍵蛋白質缺乏；在其他疾病，例如第一型肌強直症（DM1）、福克斯角膜營養不良症（FECD）和亨丁頓舞蹈症（HD）中，核苷酸重複擴展會導致產生有毒的基因產品，常與病變性核內聚焦及廣泛的剪接中斷或表現出突變蛋白質形成有毒聚體有關。我們的 GeneTAC® 小分子設計用以選擇性地針對擴展的遺傳重複序列，透過調節基因表達，根據疾病的成因，提高或降低 mRNA 轉錄，並恢復細胞健康。作為一個平台，我們認為 GeneTAC® 分子在目前尚未有治療方案的退化性、單基因核苷酸重複擴展疾病中，具有廣泛的應用潛力，影響全球數百萬人。

在針對我們 FA 項目之臨牀前研究中，我們觀察到使用我們的 FA GeneTAC® 分子後，FA 患者多種細胞類型及 FA 的小鼠模型中 frataxin（FXN）水平恢復。在觀察到在老鼠及非人類靈長類動物（NHPs）中具有良好耐受性的劑量下，FA GeneTAC® 分子在腦和心臟，這兩個受 FA 影響的關鍵器官中，達到的濃度超過在 FA 患者細胞中恢復 FXN 水平所觀察到的濃度。此外，與此有利的目標器官分佈一致，我們在 FA 的動物模型中觀察到治療後腦和心臟的內源性 FXN 表達增加。先前，我們報導了我們的 FA GeneTAC® 小分子 DT-216 在 2022 年 12 月的 Phase 1 單劑遞增（SAD）臨牀試驗及 2023 年 8 月的 Phase 1 多劑遞增（MAD）臨牀試驗的臨牀數據。兩項試驗顯示 DT-216 通常具有良好耐受性，並表現出克服導致 FA 的 FXN 轉錄障礙的能力。來自 DT-216P1 的 Phase 1 MAD 臨牀試驗數據表明，可能需要更持續的 DT-216 暴露才能達到更持久的 FXN 表達增加。我們隨後轉向開發 DT-216，以一種潛在改善的配方，以實現對 FA 的治療。這些努力導致產生了一個新的產品候選藥物 DT-216P2，其使用相同的藥物成分 DT-216。在非臨牀研究中，我們觀察到在 DT-216P2 的給藥後，DT-216 的血漿水平較 DT-216P1 的研究中更高且更持續。

DT-216P2 在正常健康志願者中進行的 Phase 1 SAD 臨牀試驗，評估單劑使用多種給藥途徑，特別是靜脈注射和皮下注射及輸注途徑，顯示 DT-216P2 通常具有良好耐受性。DT-216P2 的人體血漿藥動學（PK）曲線與 NHP 的數據一致，經靜脈注射和皮下單劑給藥後，人體 PK 數據顯示 DT-216P2 表現出較 DT-216P1 更佳的暴露和 PK 參數，包括更高的曲線下面積（AUC）及在相同劑量下持續的血漿水平。

我們正在進行 DT-216P2 的 RESTORE-FA（Reactivating Expression Suppressed Through Overcoming Repeat Expansion for FA）Phase 1/2 MAD 臨牀試驗。RESTORE-FA 試驗設計用以評估 DT-216P2 在 FA 患者中的安全性、耐受性、PK 和藥效學（PD）在靜脈注射和皮下給藥的情況。我們預計在 2026 年第二季提供 RESTORE-FA 試驗的更新，報告 DT-216P2 對內源性 frataxin 水平的影響，於 12 週給藥後的結果。
2025 年 6 月，我們收到美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）針對 DT-216P2 的 IND 申請的臨牀暫停通知。2025 年 12 月，臨牀暫停被解除，我們獲得 FDA 的批准，開始進行 DT-216P2 的臨牀試驗。

2022 年 12 月，我們提名了我們的第二個 GeneTAC® 小分子 DT-168，一種用於治療 FECD 的眼藥水。在 FECD 患者衍生的角膜內皮細胞中進行的體外測試顯示，我們的 FECD GeneTAC® 分子導致病原性核 RNA 聚焦顯著減少，並修正關鍵的錯誤剪接轉錄本至與未受影響捐贈者角膜內皮細胞中觀察到的水平相當。DT-168 在所有參與者中表現良好耐受性，且在動物模型中經眼藥水給藥後觀察到 DT-168 在角膜內及通過角膜的分佈。此外，DT-168 已經在持續九個月的慢性毒性研究中進行評估。我們認為這些非臨牀數據支持我們的新型 GeneTAC® 小分子有潛力修正 FECD 最常見的遺傳性病因。我們目前正在進行 FECD 的觀察性研究，以確認疾病特徵並評估在進行試驗時的疾病惡化情況，並識別 FECD 患者中可能有較快疾病進展風險的特徵。我們已達成觀察性研究的入組目標，透過招募並完成約 250 名 FECD 患者的基線評估。根據基線特徵數據，我們已選擇約 100 名患者進行未來的追蹤訪問。這將有助於我們的臨牀開發工作，我們認為這可能增加 DT-168 程序的成功機率。

2025 年 5 月，我們報導了已完成的 Phase 1、雙盲、安慰劑對照、隨機、SAD/MAD 臨牀試驗的結果，評估 DT-168 眼藥水在正常健康志願者中的安全性、耐受性及系統性 PK。DT-168 眼藥水在所有參與者中表現良好耐受性，最高劑量為每天兩次，每次 0.5% 的兩滴，持續七天。試驗中未觀察到嚴重不良事件、任何眼部不良事件（AEs）或因 AEs 而中止治療的情況。試驗研究者認為所有觀察到的 AEs 均與 DT-168 無關。在進行 Phase 1 試驗的同時，我們進行了參考範圍研究，顯示未受影響眼睛捐贈者與手術樣本中突變 TCF4 FECD 患者之間的角膜內皮在剪接上存在一致的不同，支持角膜內皮生物標記物作為臨牀證據的藥物活性測量潛力。我們正在進行 DT-168 的 Phase 2 生物標記物試驗，評估其在 FECD 患者中的安全性、耐受性及角膜內皮生物標記物。我們預計在 2026 年第二季報導 Phase 2 生物標記物試驗的數據。

2025 年第四季，我們宣佈 DT-818 為我們用於治療 DM1 的 GeneTAC® 小分子開發候選藥物。在臨牀前研究中，DT-818 顯示出對 DM1 具有潛在的最佳治療表現，包括在 DM1 患者細胞中，毒性 RNA 聚合體減少超過 90%，對應的剪接修正以及選擇性針對突變 DMPK。在 DM1 的 actin 重複小鼠模型（HSALR 小鼠模型）中，DT-818 治療後，肌束震顫與聚合體減少情形有所改善。在 NHP 的組織分佈研究中，DT-818 在關鍵目標組織中於耐受劑量下觀察到預期的藥理學濃度。2025 年第四季，我們獲得監管許可，啟動 DT-818 的臨牀開發，並預計在 2026 年第一季開始對 DM1 患者進行 Phase 1 MAD 研究。該研究預計於 2027 年公佈結果，將評估安全性與錯誤剪接的修正。

我們基於 GeneTAC® 平台的第四個計畫聚焦於 HD。目前我們正在進行對 HD GeneTAC® 候選分子有潛力的臨牀前研究。在 HD 患者細胞中，我們觀察到治療後，突變 huntingtin（mtHTT）mRNA 與蛋白減少，並維持野生型 huntingtin（wtHTT）。在 zQ175DN 小鼠（HD 動物模型）的體內研究中，我們觀察到在八週的全身性給藥後，腦紋狀體中 mtHTT mRNA 與蛋白減少超過 50%。在相同研究中，治療後 wtHTT mRNA 與蛋白濃度被證明維持不變。我們計畫繼續在非臨牀研究中評估這些 HD 候選分子。最終的開發候選藥物將基於在相關研究中表現良好的分子。
我們持續在臨牀前研究中推進 GeneTAC® 系列產品，以針對其他疾病並有意在這些候選藥物進展至臨牀階段時宣佈更多產品候選藥物。
我們相信 GeneTAC® 分子的結構與作用機制可能提供基因治療藥物的疾病修正潛力，同時也提供廣泛的組織分佈、修正異常基因表現並維持內生調控元件，並利用已建立的小分子製造、監管與分佈架構。
我們利用專利的 GeneTAC® 平台設計與開發由核苷酸重複擴展驅動的遺傳疾病治療候選藥物。具有核苷酸重複擴展疾病的個體出生時即擁有異常擴展的特定核苷酸序列，通常在突變基因中存在數百至數千個額外重複。更高的額外重複數量可能導致更嚴重，有時更快速進展的疾病形式。核苷酸重複擴展已被識別為影響數百萬人的超過 40 種致殘性退化疾病的基礎病因。目前尚無核准的治療選項可針對任何核苷酸重複擴展疾病的原因。

基因的特定 DNA 序列透過一種稱為轉錄的過程產生 RNA。RNA 會進一步作為模板製造控制細胞功能的蛋白質，此過程稱為翻譯。轉錄與翻譯共同負責基因表現。具有 DNA 中核苷酸重複擴展的個體可能會經歷不同的轉錄改變。在某些疾病如 FA 中，轉錄機械在異常擴展的重複序列處停滯，導致關鍵蛋白質 FXN 的產生不足。在其他情況如 DM1 中，來自核苷酸重複擴展變異的異常 RNA 轉錄物會被錯誤處理，導致一連串下游毒性與細胞功能障礙。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與本年度10-K表報中「第8項 財務報表及補充資料」所包含之財務報表及附註一併參考。除歷史資訊外，本年度報告包含前瞻性聲明，這些聲明涉及風險、不確定性與假設。我們實際結果可能與這些前瞻性聲明所預期的有重大差異，原因包括但不限於於「第1A項 風險因素」所列舉之因素。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生技製藥公司，專注於研發GeneTAC®分子，這是一種新型的小分子基因靶向嵌合體治療候選藥物，設計用以透過解決遺傳性核苷酸重複擴展突變所導致的疾病根本原因，來改變疾病的進程。某些由遺傳性核苷酸重複擴展所導致的疾病，例如弗里德里希共濟失調症（FA）與脆X症候羣，會導致基因表達減少及關鍵蛋白質缺乏；在其他疾病，例如第一型肌強直性營養不良症（DM1）、福克斯角膜營養不良症（FECD）與亨丁頓舞蹈症（HD）中，核苷酸重複擴展會導致產生有毒的基因產品，常與病變性核內聚焦及廣泛的剪接幹擾或表現出突變蛋白質形成有毒聚體有關。我們的GeneTAC®小分子設計用以選擇性地針對擴展的遺傳重複序列，根據疾病的成因，調節基因表達，透過調高或調低mRNA轉錄，並恢復細胞健康。作為一個平台，我們相信GeneTAC®分子在目前尚未有治療方案的退化性、單基因核苷酸重複擴展疾病中，具有廣泛的應用潛力，影響全球數百萬人。

在針對我們FA主要計畫的臨牀前研究中，我們觀察到使用我們的FA GeneTAC®分子後，FA患者的多種細胞類型及FA小鼠模型中，frataxin（FXN）水平得到恢復。在觀察到對老鼠及非人類靈長類（NHPs）具有良好耐受性的劑量下，FA GeneTAC®分子在腦與心臟，這兩個FA所影響的關鍵器官中，達到濃度高於觀察到能恢復FA患者細胞中FXN水平的濃度。此外，與此有利的目標器官藥物分佈一致，我們在FA小鼠模型中觀察到治療後腦與心臟的內源性FXN表達增加。先前，我們報導了我們主要的FA GeneTAC®小分子DT-216，在2022年12月的Phase 1單次劑量（SAD）臨牀試驗及2023年8月的Phase 1多劑量（MAD）臨牀試驗中的臨牀數據。兩項試驗顯示DT-216通常具有良好耐受性，並表現出克服導致FA的FXN轉錄障礙的能力。來自DT-216P1的Phase 1 MAD臨牀試驗數據表明，可能需要更長時間的DT-216暴露才能達到更持久的FXN表達增加。因此，我們轉向開發具有潛在改進配方的DT-216，以實現對FA治療的更長時間暴露。這些努力導致產生了一種新的產品候選藥物DT-216P2，其使用相同的藥物成分DT-216。在非臨牀研究中，我們觀察到在DT-216P2給藥後，DT-216的血漿濃度較DT-216P1的試驗中更高且更持久。

DT-216P2在正常健康志願者中進行的Phase 1 SAD臨牀試驗，評估單次劑量使用多種給藥途徑，特別是靜脈輸注與皮下（SC）注射及輸注途徑，顯示DT-216P2通常具有良好耐受性。DT-216P2的人類血漿藥動學（PK）曲線在靜脈及皮下單次劑量給藥後與NHP數據一致，人類PK數據顯示DT-216P2表現出較DT-216P1更佳的暴露與PK參數，包括更高的曲線下面積（AUC）及在相同劑量下更持久的血漿濃度。

我們正在進行RESTORE-FA（Reactivating Expression Suppressed Through Overcoming Repeat Expansion for FA）Phase 1/2 MAD臨牀試驗，評估DT-216P2在FA患者的安全部分、耐受性、PK及藥效學（PD）在靜脈及皮下給藥的表現。我們預計在2026年下半年根據RESTORE-FA試驗的結果，報告DT-216P2對內源性frataxin水平的影響，於12週給藥後的結果。
2025年6月，我們收到FDA針對DT-216P2 IND申請的臨牀暫停通知。2025年12月，臨牀暫停解除，我們獲得FDA批准開始進行DT-216P2的臨牀試驗。

2022年12月，我們提名了我們第二個GeneTAC®小分子DT-168，作為治療FECD的眼藥水。在FECD患者衍生的角膜內皮細胞中進行的體外測試顯示，我們的FECD GeneTAC®分子導致病原性核RNA焦點顯著減少，並修正關鍵的錯誤剪接轉錄本至與未受影響捐贈者角膜內皮細胞觀察到的水平一致。DT-168在所有參與者中表現良好耐受性，並在動物模型中觀察到DT-168在角膜內分佈。此外，DT-168已評估在持續毒性研究中，持續時間達九個月。我們認為這些非臨牀數據支持我們新型GeneTAC®小分子有潛力修正FECD最常見的遺傳性病因。我們目前正在進行FECD的觀察性研究，以確認疾病特徵並評估在進行試驗時的疾病惡化情況，並識別FECD患者中可能有更快疾病進展風險的特徵。我們已達成觀察性研究的入組目標，透過招募並完成約250名FECD患者的基線評估。根據基線特徵數據，我們選擇約100名患者進行未來的追蹤訪問。這將有助於我們的臨牀開發努力，我們認為這可能增加DT-168計畫的成功機率。

2025年5月，我們報導了已完成的Phase 1雙盲、安慰劑對照、隨機、SAD/MAD臨牀試驗結果，評估DT-168眼藥水在正常健康志願者中的安全性、耐受性及系統性PK。DT-168眼藥水在所有參與者中表現良好耐受性，最高劑量為每日兩次，每次0.5%兩滴，持續七天。試驗中沒有嚴重不良事件、沒有眼部不良事件（AEs）及因AEs而中止治療的情況。試驗研究者認為所有觀察到的AEs與DT-168無關。在進行Phase 1試驗的同時，我們進行了參考範圍研究，顯示未受影響眼捐贈者與變異TAF4 FECD患者手術樣本的角膜內皮在剪接上顯著不同，支持角膜內皮生物標記物作為臨牀概念驗證測量藥物活性的潛力。我們正在進行DT-16均的Phase 2生物標記物試驗，評估在FECD患者中的安全性、耐受性及角膜內皮生物標記物。我們預計在2026年下半年報告Phase 2生物標記物試驗的數據。

2025 年第四季，本公司宣佈 DT-818 為本公司 GeneTAC® 小分子開發候選藥物，用於治療 DM1。在臨牀前研究中，DT-818 顯示出對 DM1 具有潛在的最佳治療效果，包括在 DM1 患者細胞中，毒性 RNA 焦點減少超過 90%，對應的剪接修正與選擇性針對變異 DMPK。在 DM1 的 actin 重複小鼠模型（HSALR 小鼠模型）中，DT-818 治療後，肌束震顫與焦點減少情形有所改善。在 NHPs 的組織分佈研究中，DT-818 在關鍵目標組織中於耐受劑量下觀察到預期的藥理學濃度。2025 年第四季，本公司取得 DT-818 開始臨牀開發的監管許可，並計畫於 2026 年第一季開始對 DM1 患者進行 Phase 1 MAD 研究。該研究預計於 2027 年公佈結果，預期評估安全性與錯誤剪接修正。

我們基於 GeneTAC® 平台的第四個計畫聚焦於 HD。目前我們正在進行對 HD GeneTAC® 候選分子具有潛力的臨牀前研究。在治療 HD 患者細胞後，我們觀察到變異 huntingtin（mtHTT）mRNA 與蛋白減少，並維持野生型 huntingtin（wtHTT）。在 zQ175DN 小鼠（HD 動物模型）的體內研究中，我們觀察到在八週系統性給予 HD GeneTAC® 候選分子後，腦紋狀體中 mtHTT mRNA 與蛋白減少超過 50%。在相同研究中，治療後 wtHTT mRNA 與蛋白濃度被證明維持不變。我們計畫持續在非臨牀研究中評估這些 HD 候選分子。最終的開發候選藥物將基於在相關研究中表現良好的分子。
我們持續在臨牀前研究中推進 GeneTAC® 系列產品，以針對其他疾病並計畫在這些產品進展至臨牀階段時宣佈更多候選藥物。
我們相信 GeneTAC® 分子的結構與作用機制可能提供基因治療藥物的疾病修正潛力，同時也提供廣泛組織分佈、修正異常基因表現並維持內生調控元件，並利用現有小分子製造、監管與分佈架構。
截至目前為止，本公司自成立以來已產生淨虧損與營運現金流為負，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，累計虧損為 297.0 百萬美元。本公司淨虧損主要來自組織與僱用本公司員工、商業計畫、籌資、開發與優化技術平台、尋找潛在產品候選藥物、進行研究與非臨牀研究、臨牀開發活動、參與開發計畫的製造，以及提供一般及行政支援的費用。本公司目前尚無核准上市的產品，也尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入。
我們預期在可預見的未來，本公司費用與營運虧損將大幅增加，因我們持續進行產品候選藥物的非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗、從發現計畫中提名更多產品候選藥物，並擴展臨牀、監管、品質與製造能力，產生大量商業化費用用於行銷、銷售、製造與分銷，若我們獲得任何產品候選藥物的上市許可，以及產生與作為上市公司運作相關的額外費用。

headings: 與本公司有限營運歷史、財務狀況及資金需求相關之風險
若本公司無法在需要時籌措額外資金，可能會被迫延後、減少或終止產品開發計畫或其他營運活動。
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋、限制本公司營運活動或要求本公司放棄對智慧財產權或產品候選藥物之權利。
若本公司存放現金之金融機構發生財務問題，本公司財務狀況可能受到不利影響。
與本公司產品候選藥物之發現、開發及監管核准相關之風險
本公司產品候選藥物基於創新技術，使其難以預測產品候選藥物開發之時間、結果及成本，以及取得監管核准之可能性。
若本公司在臨牀試驗中遭遇困難或延誤納入病患，本公司之臨牀開發活動可能會延誤或受到其他不利影響。
本公司正在進行並計畫進行更多臨牀試驗以用於產品候選藥物，且這些臨牀試驗將於美國境外進行，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）可能不會接受來自這些試驗之資料。
取得並維持我方產品候選品在某一管轄區域的監管核准，並不表示我方將能成功取得我方產品候選品在其他管轄區域的監管核准。
國際貿易政策，包括關稅、制裁及貿易壁壘，可能對我方業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 本公司營運環境為動態且快速變化的，涉及許多風險與不確定性。某些因素可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響，您應謹慎考量。因此，在評估本公司業務時，我們鼓勵您考量下列所討論的風險，並配合本年度10-K表報表及其他公開檔件所載資訊。若任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果及未來成長潛力造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌。其他我們目前未預期或認為不重要的事件，也可能影響本公司營運成果與財務狀況。
本公司營運歷史有限，自成立以來已產生淨虧損，並預期未來數年仍將持續產生重大虧損。本公司可能永遠無法產生任何收入或實現盈利，或即使實現盈利，也可能無法維持。

本公司為一家臨牀階段生技製藥公司，營運歷史有限，可能使評估本公司迄今業務成功程度及未來生存能力變得困難。截至目前為止，本公司營運活動僅限於商業規劃、組織及僱用員工、籌措資金、發展及優化技術平台、識別潛在產品候選藥物、針對FA主要計畫及其他開發計畫進行研究及非臨牀研究、FA、FECD及DM1計畫的早期臨牀開發、建立及強化智慧財產權組合，以及提供這些營運活動的一般及行政支援。因此，本公司任何產品候選藥物尚未獲得商業銷售許可。本公司從未因產品銷售產生任何收入，且自開始營運以來，每年均產生淨虧損，包括截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日止年度的淨虧損為69.8 百萬美元及49.6 百萬美元。本公司預期在取得產品候選藥物的監管批准及商業化之前，將需數年時間，若能實現的話。本公司預期在未來數年內及可預見的未來，營運虧損將持續增加。本公司過去的虧損，加上預期未來的虧損，已對股東權益及營運資金產生並持續產生負面影響。

要成為並持續保持盈利，本公司必須開發並最終商業化具有重大市場潛力的產品或產品羣。這將需要本公司成功完成產品候選物的非臨牀研究及臨牀試驗、取得這些產品候選物的市場批准、製造、行銷及銷售這些產品（若本公司取得市場批准），並符合任何上市後的相關要求。本公司可能永遠無法成功完成這些活動，即使成功商業化一個或數個產品候選物，本公司也可能永遠無法產生足夠且重要的收入以實現盈利。此外，作為一家年輕企業，本公司可能面臨預期之外的費用、困難、複雜問題、延誤及其他已知或未知的挑戰。若本公司實現盈利，也可能無法維持或提高季度或年度的盈利，並持續產生大量研究與開發及其他支出以開發及行銷更多產品候選物。本公司若無法成為並持續保持盈利，將降低公司價值，並可能影響本公司籌資能力、維持研究與開發工作、擴展業務或持續營運。公司價值的下降也可能導致您損失全部或部分投資。
自成立以來，本公司已使用大量現金以支應營運，並預期未來數年內營運費用將大幅增加。生物科技產品候選物的開發屬於高成本性質。當產品候選物進入並推進至非臨牀研究及臨牀試驗階段時，本公司將需要大量額外資金以擴展臨牀、監管、品質及製造能力。此外，若本公司取得任何產品候選物的市場批准，預期將產生大量商業化費用，包括行銷、銷售、製造及分銷相關支出。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司現金、現金等價物及投資證券為219.8百萬美元。根據目前營運計畫，本公司估計現有現金、現金等價物及投資證券足以支應營運費用及資本支出需求超過12個月。然而，本公司認為現有現金、現金等價物及投資證券不足以支應任何產品候選物至監管批准，並將需要籌集大量額外資金以完成產品候選物的開發與商業化。
